stages.name: Native Runtime Dedup
stages.result: No production duplicate Native runtime was proven; no R5 code diff was justified.

stages.name: Manual / Automation Decouple
stages.result: Ordinary Manual Native operation is Automation-independent and Product Project identity remains separate from AutomationProject; no R6 code diff was justified.

stages.name: Projection / Map
stages.exit: Map connects Workbench governance and native/runtime/provider/resource references as a useful projection without becoming execution or workflow truth.

conclusions: Ordinary GUI startup does not initialize Automation unless explicitly activated.
Manual Native Thread/Turn IPC does not require Automation workflow/governance state.
Product ProjectRecord is owned by V1 Workbench persistence.
AutomationProject is owned by independent Automation persistence.
Requirement and Planner operations require an existing AutomationProject.
No automatic Product Project to AutomationProject identity collapse was found.
Legacy WORKBENCH_PROJECT ExternalRef kind is provider workflow scope carrier vocabulary, not V1 Project ownership.

frozenInvariants: Do not persist a duplicate transcript.
Manual V1 remains independent of Automation.
Workbench Project remains distinct from AutomationProject.
RequirementVersion and PlanVersion remain Workbench governance truth.
Unknown external side effects reconcile instead of blind resend.
WebGPT exact-target actions fail closed when target identity cannot be proven.
Evidence/Audit do not own workers or resource leases.
Map is a Workbench incremental projection and is not duplicate native planning.
Do not implement a second sandbox, tool runtime, or subagent runtime.
resumeProtocol: Read HANDOFF.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, GIT_WORKFLOW.md, R5_NATIVE_RUNTIME_AUDIT.md, R6_MANUAL_AUTOMATION_AUDIT.md, and R7_AUDIT_TARGETS.md.
Verify current workbench/next and relevant remote refs before trusting stored checkpoint values.
